title: Executable evidence contracts
thesis: [INFERENCE] Use executable decision worlds to separate factual intervention, untrusted direction, and authenticated policy changes with exact outcome labels.
prior_work: [EXT] SecFid already separates fidelity from injection resistance; Executable Counterfactuals already provides executable causal reasoning tasks.
novelty_check: [INFERENCE] Neither executable counterfactuals nor retention is new. Candidate contribution: a typed intervention contract, held-out event composition and budgeted adaptive attacks. Fully observed event edits are interventions, not causal abduction.
gap: [INFERENCE] Exact decision-update labels with independent oracles instead of same-family model agreement.
asset_edge: [EXT: ours] Card paired controls, AgentDojo predicates and the documented evidence-label bottleneck.
cpu_first: [INFERENCE] Enumerate 200 small worlds and four interventions using independently specified interpreters; measure oracle disagreement, answer balance and behavioral collisions. No model inference.
first_paid: [INFERENCE] One-hour capped pilot: 100 worlds x four variants x two existing judge arms, plus reserved adaptive subset. Full confirmation and human wording audit are extra.
cost_basis: [INFERENCE] Estimated pilot envelope = H100 wall-hour cap x stipulated $3.95/h, including startup; throughput unverified; not spent or authorized.
risk: [INFERENCE] Lexical toy, invalid prose realization, or duplication of SecFid.
funder_fit: [INFERENCE] EA Funds Transformative AI Fund; Foresight Coordination and accountability, independent assessment track.
score_basis: [INFERENCE] V*P/(1+H); subjective priorities, not observed probabilities; labor and annotation excluded.
methodology: [INFERENCE] Four grammars; 400 independent worlds x four matched contract arms; primary joint success, secondary clean accuracy, steering, evidence response and policy response. Cluster by world; hold out compositional rules. Negative controls ignore all evidence or follow last directive. Blind two-human audit of 40 prose realizations before scoring.
sample_size: [INFERENCE] Paired-binary approximation n=7.84*q/delta^2 gives about 235 at q=.30, delta=.10; plan 400 before clustering. Four grammars do not constitute 400 independent domains.
kill_conditions: [INFERENCE] Unresolved oracle disagreement; >5% invalid prose; >90% lexical-control performance; no composition separation; or equivalent SecFid contract already exists.
status: [MEAS] Literature only; no experiment or paid step executed. Source metadata and full methodology are in README.md.

title: Backdoor behavior x presentation crossover
thesis: [INFERENCE] Cross minimal behavioral repair with semantics-preserving presentation changes to distinguish monitor sensitivity to defects from sensitivity to cues.
prior_work: [EXT] SLEIGHT-Bench pairs malicious/benign transcripts; SemTrace studies semantic sensitivity; SET-based attacks use semantics-preserving transformations.
novelty_check: [INFERENCE] Matched variants and semantic sensitivity are already done. Candidate contribution is a functionally validated within-program APPS 2x2 causal comparison, not another static artifact classifier.
gap: [INFERENCE] Isolate behavioral discrimination from presentation sensitivity with validated repairs and held-out transformation families.
asset_edge: [EXT: ours] Assignment supplies 162 verified backdoored and 573 honest APPS programs with trigger/reference evidence; counts not reverified here.
cpu_first: [INFERENCE] Construct static candidate crossovers for 20 programs; check parsing, variable binding and repair feasibility. Static checks do not establish semantic equivalence; later execution only in existing no-network sandbox.
first_paid: [INFERENCE] One-hour monitor pilot of at most 162 x four cells x two arms = 1296 scores, only after sandbox and human validity gates.
cost_basis: [INFERENCE] H100 wall-hour cap x stipulated $3.95/h; includes startup, excludes annotation/sandbox engineering; throughput unverified; not spent.
risk: [INFERENCE] Ambiguous repair, invalid trigger domain, small independent-problem count or surface changes that alter behavior.
funder_fit: [INFERENCE] EA Funds Transformative AI Fund; Foresight independent technical assessment.
methodology: [INFERENCE] Attempt every backdoor without monitor selection. Four cells: defective/repaired x original/transformed. Validate provided tests, trigger and fresh domain-valid inputs in sandbox. Primary paired suspicion contrast; secondary interaction, discrimination and detection at frozen FPR. Identity/comment/format controls. Split by APPS problem; reserve one third of honest programs for final evaluation.
sample_size: [INFERENCE] Paired delta=.15, discordance=.40 requires about 140 independent pairs before clustering by n=7.84*q/delta^2. At 60 pairs detectable delta is about .23. Maximum 162 programs is not 162 independent problems; low-FPR estimates remain imprecise.
kill_conditions: [INFERENCE] Fewer than 60 feasible independent problems for target; invalid trigger domains; repair labels leak; tested semantics change; or no insight beyond static artifact audit and existing matched benchmarks.

title: Oversight-queue availability frontier
thesis: [INFERENCE] Measure adversarial consumption of pre-execution review capacity and equal-resource admission policies that preserve legitimate service without increasing harmful release.
prior_work: [EXT] AgentDoS establishes resource exhaustion; SLEIGHT discusses review feasibility; adaptive control protocols already have finite audit budgets.
novelty_check: [INFERENCE] Resource denial and finite oversight are established. Narrow contribution: pre-execution human-review queue frontier with host-enforced holds, not token exhaustion or post-hoc review.
gap: [INFERENCE] Quantify availability and starvation under review-inducing floods at equal staffing/storage with explicit identity assumptions.
asset_edge: [EXT: ours] Fail-closed saturation semantics, receipt events and AgentDojo routing traces; local proposition identifies missing service model.
cpu_first: [INFERENCE] Event-driven synthetic replay with 100000 arrivals per scenario, bursty attackers and finite reviewers; compare FIFO, per-principal fair queues and reserved capacity including identity splitting.
first_paid: [INFERENCE] One-hour fresh AgentDojo trace pilot to replace synthetic routing frequencies. Structural queue analysis needs no GPU.
cost_basis: [INFERENCE] One H100 wall-hour x stipulated $3.95/h; includes startup, excludes human-service measurement; not spent.
risk: [INFERENCE] Unrealistic service times or identity assumptions explain all benefit; result only restates overload.
funder_fit: [INFERENCE] Foresight Human Empowerment/decentralized oversight; EA Funds Transformative AI Fund.
methodology: [INFERENCE] Sweep utilization .25,.50,.75,.95,1.10; burst/sustained attack, service variability and capacity; authenticated vs freely split identities. Matched reviewers/storage across policies. Primary legitimate deadline completion; co-primary harmful effects; secondary p95 wait, starvation, review work and cost to halve completion. Controls: no attack, infinite service, always hold, explicitly unsafe fail-open.
sample_size: [INFERENCE] 100 independent schedules per declared cell with shared random numbers across policies. At assumed paired SD .10, SE=.01. Schedules, not arrivals, are replication units. Paired bootstrap and correction for frozen policy family; simulation does not measure human behavior.
kill_conditions: [INFERENCE] Benefit vanishes under realistic identity splitting/service times; relies on auto-approval; or offers no frontier improvement or falsifiable operational constraint.
status: [MEAS] Literature only; no simulations or experiments executed.
